The graph above shows $y=k({10}^{x})+c.$ Determine the values of $k$ and $c$ and find the equation of the curve.
question.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote of the curve $y=k({10}^{x})+c$ is $y=c.$ In the graph above, the horizontal asymptote is $y=-3,$ so $c=-3.$

Therefore, our function takes the form

$$
y=k({10}^{x})-3.
$$

We can solve for $k$ by finding a point on the graph and substituting for $x$ and $y.$ The labeled point on the graph is $(0,1),$ so we substitute $x=0$ and $y=1$ into the function and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =k({10}^{x})-3 \\ 1 & =k({10}^{0})-3 \\ 1 & =k(1)-3 \\ 1 & =k-3 \\ 4 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curve is $y=4({10}^{x})-3.$
